title: UK Actors Demand Legal Voice Rights as AI Cloning Scams Hit 28%
desc: 80 UK actors ask the PM to make voice a statutory right as cloning scams reach 28% of adults. What the campaign means for firms using AI voice agents.
keywords: ai voice cloning uk, save our voices now campaign, voice cloning scams, ai voice agent compliance, voice cloning law uk
cta: Want a compliant AI voice agent built?
body:
August 29, 2026. Around 80 UK actors, comedians, and artists, including Hugh Bonneville, Nicola Coughlan, Siobhan McSweeney, Matt Lucas, and Luke Evans, have signed an open letter to Prime Minister Andy Burnham asking the government to make a person's voice a protected statutory right, as reported this week, backed by a petition on the government's own site. The campaign, Save Our Voices Now, says a voice can be convincingly cloned from about three seconds of audio and cites research that 28 percent of UK adults report being targeted by a voice cloning scam. For business owners this is not celebrity news. The same three seconds applies to any founder who has ever posted a podcast, a webinar, or a video ad, and the scam wave is already changing how customers answer calls from businesses, including legitimate automated ones.

What the Campaign Is Asking For

  1. Statutory ownership of voice: legal protection for a person's voice as part of their identity, similar to the protection already available for a name or image, requested through an open letter to the Prime Minister and a Gov.uk petition, per PA Media reporting.
  2. The trigger is speed: campaign founder Peter Caulfield says a voice can be cloned, stolen, and reinterpreted without the speaker's knowledge from seconds of audio, and modern systems can then generate statements the speaker never made.
  3. There is precedent: Denmark has moved toward giving individuals legal rights over their face, body, and voice, including the ability to demand removal of unauthorized synthetic media, so the UK ask follows an existing European direction rather than inventing one.

The Numbers Behind the Alarm

The 28 percent figure is campaign cited survey research rather than government data, but it matches the pattern fraud teams describe: voice cloning converts an ordinary invoice scam into an authority scam. A cloned founder voice calling the bookkeeper about an urgent supplier payment defeats the skepticism that a strange email no longer survives. The same erosion cuts the other way. As more people assume an unexpected voice might be synthetic, pickup rates and trust drop for every business calling customers, which raises the bar for anyone deploying AI callers commercially. Disclosure stops being a legal nicety and becomes the thing that keeps your calls answered.

What It Means for Operators

Play defense first. Institute a verification rule for any voice request that moves money or credentials: call back on a known number or require a pre agreed code word, with no exceptions for urgency, and brief whoever pays your invoices, because urgency is the scam's engine. Assume your own founder's voice is publicly clonable and make sure a three second clip cannot authorize anything at your company. Then deploy responsibly. If you run AI voice agents for intake, follow up, or booking, disclose that the caller is an AI at the start of the call, put any cloned or licensed brand voice in writing with consent, keep a human handoff path, and log it all, because the UK campaign, Denmark's rules, and the US state patchwork all point in the same direction. The legal side of automated calling is mapped in our guide to whether AI cold calling is legal, and compliance first voice automation is exactly what we build inside our AI automation practice. Regulation is coming for voice AI in Tier 1 markets, and the operators who build consent and disclosure in now will be the ones still calling when it lands.
faqs: What is the Save Our Voices Now campaign?

It is a UK campaign backed by around 80 actors, comedians, and artists, including Hugh Bonneville, Nicola Coughlan, Siobhan McSweeney, Matt Lucas, and Luke Evans, asking the UK government to recognize a person's voice as a protected statutory right. It combines an open letter to Prime Minister Andy Burnham with a petition on Gov.uk.
Can a voice really be cloned from three seconds of audio?

The campaign says a voice can be convincingly cloned from about three seconds of audio with the right AI system, and modern speech models can generate new statements in that voice which the speaker never made. Any founder or executive with public audio online, from podcasts to video ads, should assume their voice can be replicated.
Is AI voice cloning illegal in the UK right now?

There is currently no dedicated UK statutory right to a person's voice, which is what the campaign wants to change. Existing routes such as passing off, data protection, and fraud law cover some misuse, and Denmark has moved toward explicit rights over face, body, and voice, a direction campaigners want the UK to follow. This is general information, not legal advice.
How should businesses using AI voice agents respond?

Disclose that a caller is an AI at the start of the call, get written consent and licensing for any cloned brand voice, keep a human handoff path, and log consent and disclosures. Separately, protect against incoming voice fraud with a callback or code word rule for any request that moves money or credentials, since cloned authority voices are the fastest growing version of the invoice scam.
